name: a contributor is told whether anybody can find them, and what is left
description:
ADR-0022. The rules that decide whether a hirer can see somebody live in the search query — `overall_score IS NOT NULL`, the lapse comparison, the availability gate — and until now a contributor could satisfy every field on their screen and still appear in no result anywhere, with nothing telling them why.

Two kinds of answer, and keeping them apart is the point. A BLOCKER means no hirer can find you at all. A LIMIT means you are findable and a whole class of role cannot reach you. Flattening the two into one list would present an urgent thing and a deliberate choice as the same thing — the same mistake as showing a lapsed window and an opt-out alike.

THE ONE PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW ABOUT is no_scored_claim. Search reads overall_score, so somebody who set availability and filled in every field is still invisible until a claim of theirs has been judged. Alice below is exactly that person, and every step she takes leaves it in place.

This replaces profile_matchable_needs_both_halves, which asserted the composition rule ADR-0021 removed: a live window with nothing ticked used to match nobody. It cannot now, so the case it pinned no longer exists.

steps._step: Alice has answered nothing. Her window is live, so availability is not the problem — and she is still findable by nobody, because no claim of hers has been scored. Four limits sit underneath, each naming a class of role that cannot reach her.
She fills in what she can. Three limits clear and the BLOCKER does not — which is the honest answer, and the one the old screen could not give: there is nothing left on this page for her to do.

CAROL'S WINDOW LAPSED YESTERDAY, and that is a second blocker beside the unscored claim. Lapsed is not an opt-out — she is still ranked and one click from returning — but a hirer searching by default does not see her.

BOB OPTED OUT, and is told so rather than nagged. It is a decision he made and it is working — no hirer toggle reveals him (ADR-0008 §1a) — so the screen owes him the fact that it is in force, not a prompt to undo it.
